• Output 1.1. Communication protocol between L1 and L2
Midgard’s L2 consensus protocol operates via a collection of smart contracts on L1 and a data availability layer. These smart contracts implement the mechanisms by which L1-based user events are generated, operators’ L2 blocks are sequenced and confirmed in the L1 state queue, and fraudulent blocks are removed.
• Output 1.2. L2 transaction handling

Transaction validation is handled optimistically in Midgard. This means that the current operator gathers all the transactions received via the L2 API (and those ordered via L1) into a block and commits the block’s header to the Midgard state queue on L1. ・Midgard outbox smart contract 
・Midgard inbox smart contract

The checkpoint mechanism evolved greatly to inherit more security from the Cardano L1 then what was possible in the original milestone
The event inbox is the set of events received from the L1 blockchain by the Midgard L2.
The block producer will receive a list of events from the L1 by some relayer, and then include the merkle root of the events in the block header.
There are two types of events that can be received from the L1:
Messages - these contain arbitrary information sent from Cardano L1 to the Midgard L2. This information can be used to move assets from Cardano to Midgard or to communicate other information about events on Cardano to Midgard. 
Transactions - These are transactions that are submitted on the Cardano L1 that must be executed in the Midgard L2. This "Forced Transaction Inclusion" is a security feature that allows participants of the Midgard network to access their funds in the (unlikely) event that Midgard block production is compromised or malicious, e.g. the block producer is censoring transactions. This is one of the powerful mechanisms through which Midgard inherits Cardano's security.

ms.report:
We are pleased to submit the Proof of Achievement for Milestone 4 of the Midgard: Cardano Layer 2 project.
Milestone 4 delivers the on-chain smart contracts that govern how users interact with the Midgard Layer 2 from Layer 1 (Cardano preprod). The inbox contracts handle user deposits and transaction orders entering the L2; the outbox contracts govern withdrawals and settlement of finalized L2 state back to L1. All contracts are implemented in Aiken (Plutus v3) and have been deployed and exercised on Cardano preprod across the 2026-04-25 operator/state-commitment run and the 2026-05-08 withdrawal/payout run.
A. Output: Deposit Contract (Inbox)
Users can lock ADA and native assets into the Midgard L2 via a validated deposit transaction. Contract deployed on Cardano preprod testnet.
Acceptance criteria: Contract is published on GitHub, compiles successfully, and users can submit verified deposit transactions to the Midgard inbox on preprod.
Evidence: Source code — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/onchain/aiken/validators/user-events/deposit.ak | Preprod contract address: addr_test1wpuzy7pa0a2n5fddn5vuzua07nha28pug9l2w8l9v3vlxsg8mw2hg | On-chain deposit tx (2026-04-25): https://preprod.cardanoscan.io/transaction?id=637291210692b6b00edf9f09acf11a8fdd25c75eca4115c0f0ec718676c5528a
B. Output: Transaction Order Contract (Inbox)
Users can submit L2 transactions via the tx-order contract, which queues them for inclusion in the next L2 block. Phase 1 (deserialization) and phase 2 validations are applied on receipt. Contract deployed on preprod.
Acceptance criteria: Contract is published on GitHub, compiles successfully, and tx-order submissions are validated and accepted by the Midgard node on preprod.
Evidence: Source code — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/onchain/aiken/validators/user-events/tx-order.ak | Preprod contract address: addr_test1wryh5c33n27qu9nu4smrd9a3

ms.report:
We are pleased to submit the Proof of Achievement for Milestone 5 of the Midgard: Cardano Layer 2 project.
Milestone 5 delivers the Midgard Node MVP requirements listed in the Catalyst portal: network parameterization configurations, the Layer 2 toolkit for managing node services, Docker infrastructure for deployment and management of Layer 2 nodes, and an API provider service for data retrieval and transaction submission. The node connects to Cardano L1 through Kupmios or Blockfrost, monitors user-event contract addresses, batches L2 transactions into blocks, commits state to the on-chain state queue, and exposes a REST API. On 2026-04-25 the node drove a full protocol run on Cardano preprod, producing two state commitments and a state merge.
A. Output: Network Parameterization Configurations
Configuration files and parameter sources define the network, L1 provider, persistence, operator, and protocol settings used by the Midgard node. The Docker and local run paths both start from the published environment and config sources.
Acceptance criteria: Network parameterization is implemented in the repository and can be reviewed through the published configuration files and protocol parameter sources. The preprod protocol run demonstrates that the chosen parameters supported node operation without non-malicious-user outage during the cited test run.
Evidence: Environment parameter template — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/demo/midgard-node/.env.example | Runtime config service — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/demo/midgard-node/src/services/config.ts | SDK protocol parameters — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/demo/midgard-sdk/src/protocol-parameters.ts | On-chain protocol parameters — https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/midgard/blob/367ede9ae356ef4da0f0fb45b7eedc59c64585d6/onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/protoco
